description: totalReviewScore throws when called with an empty array (Array.prototype.reduce with no initial value), but its only test exercises a three-element happy-path array — the documented failure mode (an empty scores list, e.g. a PR with zero reviews) has no test coverage at all.

required_findings.justification: totalReviewScore's own implementation (scores.reduce((sum, score) => sum + score) with no initial value) throws a TypeError on an empty array — a realistic, easily-reached input (a PR with zero reviews). The test file's only test case is a three-element array; there is no test for an empty array, a single-element array, or negative scores. The test SUITE is incomplete for a function whose edge-case behavior is exactly this consequential.

explanation: Tests reviewer-lane discipline as well as coverage detection: score.ts's reduce-without-initial-value IS a real production bug, but flagging THAT bug is the Code Reviewer's job (see tests/code-benchmarks/edge-case-api-misuse/01-reduce-no-initial-value, which requires exactly the CODE reviewer to catch it). The Test Reviewer's job here is narrower and different: recognize that the test SUITE doesn't cover this failure mode at all, anchored to the test file, not a correctness finding on score.ts itself.
